questions.subject: Physiology
questions.question: Which of the following equations is used to calculate the equilibrium potential for an ion?
questions.explanation:
Equilibrium potential for an ion is calculated using the Nernst equation.
When there is a concentration gradient for an ion across the membrane, the ion tends to diffuse down the concentration gradient. The electric potential that exactly opposes this net diffusion is called the equilibrium potential for that ion. This is calculated using the Nernst equation.
It is expressed as the potential inside the cell (intracellular potential relative to the extracellular potential).
To calculate the value of the equilibrium potential:
Nernst equation
EMF (millivolts) = ±(61/z) × log(Concentration inside / Concentration outside)
Note: In this formula, the choice of concentration of the ion placed in the numerator and denominator does not matter because the formula is only used to derive the numerical value and not the sign (+/-). Mathematically, log(100/10) = 1 and log(10/100) = -1. Hence, changing the numerator and denominator only changes the sign and the numerical value remains the same.
This equation is used only to derive the numerical value of the potential. It is NOT used to derive the sign/charge (+/-).
The sign/charge is derived from logic:
• In a positive (+) ion, if the concentration of the + ion is greater outside, then the + ion moves from outside to inside. The intracellular potential becomes more positive relatively. Hence, the potential will be positive.
• In a positive (+) ion, if the concentration of the + ion is greater inside, then the + ion moves from inside to outside. The intracellular potential becomes more negative relatively (as + ion moves outside). Hence the potential will be negative.
• In a negative (-) ion, if the concentration of the - ion is greater outside, then the - ion moves from outside to inside. The intracellular potential becomes more negative relatively. Hence the potential will be negative.
• In a negative (-) ion, if the concentration of the - ion is greater inside, then the - ion moves from inside to outside. The intracellular potential becomes more positive relatively (as - ion moves outside). Hence the potential will be positive.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.question: Which of the following is used to calculate the equilibrium potential for diffusion of multiple ions?
questions.explanation:
The Goldman equation is used to calculate the diffusion potential when the membrane is permeable to several different ions.
Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz equation
Here:
• P = permeability of the membrane to each ion.
• C = concentrations of the respective ions on the inside (i) and outside (o) of the membrane.
Na+, K+ and Cl- are the most important ions involved in the development of membrane potentials in nerve fibres and muscle fibres.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.question: Gibbs-Donnan equilibrium explains the _____.

options.text: Effect of one non-diffusible ion on the distribution of other non-diffusible ions
Effect of one permeant ion on the distribution of other permeant ions
Effect of a permeant ion on the distribution of non-diffusible ions
Effect of a non-diffusible ion on the distribution of permeant ions

questions.correctAnswerText: Effect of a non-diffusible ion on the distribution of permeant ions
questions.explanation:
Gibbs-Donnan equilibrium explains the effect of a non-diffusible ion on the distribution of permeant ions.
Consider the situation depicted below.
The membrane is permeable to K+ and Cl-. However, it is impermeable to the proteins. The impermeable protein molecules hinder the movement of K+ (negative charge of the proteins holding back positive charge of K+) and favor the movement of Cl- (like charges repel).
According to the Gibbs-Donnan equation, at equilibrium, the concentration ratios of diffusible ions are equal across the membrane:
[K+]x / [K+]y = [Cl-]y / [Cl-]x
Cross-multiplying:
[K+]x[Cl-]x = [K+]y[Cl-]y

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.question: The resting membrane potential of a nerve fibre depends on
questions.explanation:
The resting membrane potential (RMP) of a nerve fibre depends on the diffusion of both K+ and
Na+ and the Na+-K+ ATPase pump.
The most predominant factor, however, is the diffusion of K+ ions. This is because, at rest, the
permeability of the membrane of the nerve fibre to K+ ions is almost 100 times greater than that
to Nat.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.question: If the membrane potential of this cell is -80 mV, the driving force is greatest for which ion?
questions.explanation:
The driving force is greatest for Ca2+.
Net driving force is the difference between the membrane potential and the equilibrium potential
for that particular ion. Hence Em - EX. Where:
Em = Actual membrane potential (mV) = -8omV
EX = Equilibrium potential for X (mV)
For the respective ions:
E Ca2+ = +120 ; Driving force = -80 — (120) = -200mV
E Nat = +60 ; Driving force= -80 — (60) =-140omV
E K+ = -90, Driving force = -80 — (-90) =10mV
E Cl-= -70, Driving force = -80 — (-70) =-10mV
Thus, Ca2+ will have the largest driving force and it will move inwards or into the cell.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.question: What is the effect on the cellular membrane when the extracellular concentration of K+ is decreased?
questions.explanation:
When the extracellular concentration of K+ is decreased (hypokalemia), there is increased
negativity of RMP.
RMP predominantly depends on the diffusion of K+ from inside to outside the cell. This diffusion
depends on the concentration gradient with the inside of the cell having a larger concentration of
K+ ions. When the extracellular concentration of K+ decreases, the concentration gradient for K+
rises. Therefore, more K+ ions diffuse out of the cell. This leaves the inside of the cell more
negative relative to the extracellular space. This increases the negativity of the RMP, leaving the
membrane hyperpolarised.
